item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: C. Emlen Urban & The Chocolate King — Thu Nov 19, 5:30 PM — LancasterHistory Museum & Research Center
item.description:
One built an empire with a Kiss and the other designed it. This is the untold story of Milton S. Hershey and his architect, C. Emlen Urban. What drove these two men to achieve goals and fame beyond their wildest dreams? Why is one an American icon and the other unknown beyond his hometown? Drawn from his new book, Urban and the Chocolate King, architect and historian Gregg Scott joins LancasterHistory to tell the tale of two men who met as young boys in the small town of Lancaster, PA, and began a journey of design and construction that endured for fifty years.
Gregg Scott is a Fellow of the American Institute of Architects, a partner emeritus and co-founder of RLPS Architects, a monthly columnist for LNP, and twice recipient of the Journalist and Educators Award presented by the Historic Preservation Trust of Lancaster County. Most recently, the author of Urban Legend, Urban Alphabet, and the 2026 fall release of Urban and the Chocolate King.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lanc

item.title: PDF@Zoetropolis Presents Minari — Thu Nov 19, 6:30 PM — Zoetropolis Cinema Stillhouse
item.description:
Our November America 250 selection, Lee Isaac Chung’s Minari, follows a Korean American family pursuing a new life on a small Arkansas farm in the early 1980s.
It is a deeply American story of immigration, land, work, faith, family, and reinvention—but also a searching examination of the costs hidden within the American dream. Who bears the burden of one person’s ambition? Does independence ever exist without care and dependency? What transforms a piece of land into a home?
Arriving during harvest and Thanksgiving season, Minari also asks us to think about cultivation and gratitude: whose labor sustains a family, whose histories inhabit the land, and what conditions allow transplanted lives to flourish. Its answer is both modest and profound: nothing grows entirely on its own.
Learn More
Source: Fig Lancaster

item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: An Intro to Poetry (For those who don't like poetry) with Caroline Covington — Fri Nov 13, 7:00 PM — The Trust Performing Arts Center
item.description:
The Row House Forum welcomes Caroline Covington to speak on “An Introduction to Poetry (For those who don’t like poetry)” in The Square Halo Gallery of the Trust Performing Arts Center.
Ms. Covington is a Lancaster native, now living on Maryland’s Eastern Shore. As an undergraduate she studied nursing, Bible, and music. In graduate school she focused on the intellectual history of the Church and how historical moments affect theology and Christian practice. Currently Caroline fills her days gardening, knitting, cooking, talking on the phone with family and friends, and working alongside her husband, Will, caring for their 1790s home. And enjoying poetry, of course. She’ll give a jump start on appreciating poems by sharing her relatively newfound appreciation and by reading some of her faves. Even those who already love poetry will enjoy an inspiring evening of ideas, tea, and finger foods.
Register Now

item.title: Evening Compline — Mon Nov 16, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
